questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A big priority for me was to go to an english-speaking country so there would not be a language barrier between me and my co-student. Also I wanted to explore parts of the world outside of Europe, therefore I narrowed my choices down to USA, Australia and New Zealand. In all countries I could find relevant academic courses such that I still could follow my degree. In the end I choose Australia because it was so different to anywhere I have already been.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I am so glad I choose to go on exchange it was a beriching experience and I would recommend it to everybody who was the opportunity.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: This was really easy. The university I choose (Monash) send me all the relevant information needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were an oriantation week before the study started. In this week I got tons of practical information and more importantly I got to meet other exchange student. In addition to this week there were a dedicated information center on campus where you could get help with almust anything from housing to public transport.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through Corporate Keys which was recommend by the university. The process of finding the right place was a bit difficult as you could only see pictures of the places you were interested in. However when I did find the right place the process was fairly easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I found a place really close to campus which I am really happy I did. I lived so close I walked to school every day. Melbourne is a really big city and public transport is not as good as in Copenhagen, so many students spent over an hour just to get to campus. 

I would recommend living close to campus, because there is a lot of activities on campus which will be harder to get to if you live in the city. You can always go to the city in the weekends which is nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is really expensive to live in Melbourne. I found it more expensive then Copenhagen.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Monash University took care of almost everything. I only needed to make up a password for my account and set up a verification app on my phone.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were a helpdesk on campus and an e-mail address you could write to. The respond quick on mails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: From home I searched for preapproval on 6 different classes and were accepted on all of them. I then choose 4 different classes to begin with. The first 3 weeks of the semester is kinda a "trial run" on the classes as you have the chance to reregister classs. I actually did this and it was easy to do, you just have to self-study on the weeks you missed.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: At Monash you choose some timeslots where you place your classes. Be quick to do this as the good timeslot gets filled up quick.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses are lower then at Copenhagen University however the workload during the semester was greater at Monash University, which means you will have more assignments and quizes then at Copenhagen University. Everything you hand in at Monash University will count to your final grade.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more or less similar. You have to read before the lecture on the topic of the day. After the lecture you will have exercises which is considered homework if not done in the allocated exercise-class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
NEURAL NETWORKS AND DEEP LEARNING
MACHINE LEARNING
INTRODUCTION TO DATABASES
ALGORITHMS AND PROGRAMMING FOUNDATIONS IN
 PYTHON

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: My favorite course was NEURAL NETWORKS AND DEEP LEARNING. The teaching staff was great at interacting with the student, the exercises were carefully made and the topic was interesting to me. The other courses were also great however this course just stands out to me.

questions.answer: I do not feel like I encountered unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee in Melbourne is great and cheap. I was surprised of the housing prices.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were all sort of sports- and socialclubs you could enroll in. At the orientation week all of these clubs were presented.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Follow Monash Student Association (MSA) and Monash Graduate Association (MGA) on instagram to find great and fun acitivties through out the week, most of these event are free or fairly cheap.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There a many great places in Australia. Close to Melbounre are Grampions, Phillip Island, Wilsons prom and great ocean road which i recommend. Also in some weekend flights are fairly cheap so go a weekend to Sydney or book a trip to Uluru. Tasmania is also close and a beautiful place.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. The culture is not that different from Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open, attend the events and be the one who takes initiative to talk to others.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Australiens use a lot of slang and shortening of words that you have to get used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their openness and politeness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Use the campus facillities and explore the campus life.
Do not get to caught up in school as there are many other increadible things to learn and explore.
Make new friends and meaningful connections.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy your stay, even in the tough periods. It is over before you know it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in another country and you are forced to make new friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balance school, social-life and exploring the country.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
